feature: Reset each transform mode on its own
summary: Right-click a button on the selection chip to reset just that kind of change (size, skew and distort, or 3D) or all of them, and see at a glance which modes you have changed by the small dot on their chip buttons. The same rows and Turn in 3D sit under Edit > Transform.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: reset-each-transform-mode-walk (pointer, right click on the chip) and transform-resets-from-the-menu-walk (Edit > Transform, takes the front).

try.do: Drop a screenshot on a picture and click it: no chip button wears a dot. Right-click the chip: all four Reset rows are grey.
Stretch it with the right pill and turn it with the knob: the Size button gets a blue dot.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click Skew & distort and drag the top pill, then click 3D and drag the right pill: every button has a dot, white on the picked one.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right-click the chip: Reset Size, Reset Skew & Distort, Reset 3D, then Reset All.
Choose Reset Size: the picture is its own size and upright about the same middle, still skewed and tipped, and the tag says Reset Size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command-Z, then choose Reset Skew & Distort and then Reset 3D from the chip's right click: each takes only its own dot.
Open Edit > Transform: Turn in 3D under Keystone, then the four resets above the flips. Choose Reset All.

evaluate: Is the dot enough to tell you, without reading anything, which kinds of change a picture carries?
Does Reset Size putting a pasted screenshot back at its full pixel size feel right, even when it was scaled down to fit when it landed?
Is it right that a shape or text has no size to go back to, so Reset Size only takes away its turn?
Does the tag saying Reset Size for a second tell you enough that it worked?
rough: The menu row reads Reset Skew & Distort, where the prototype prints Reset Skew & distort: every menu row is Title Case (UX-PATTERNS §7). The chip's own tooltip still says Skew & distort.

The rows live in Edit > Transform, where the prototype's panel heads them Layer > Transform: the app's one Transform submenu is in Edit, where Photoshop keeps it, as chosen when Skew and Distort landed (skew-distort-reshapes-the-picture-from-the-selec). The Layer menu's Reset 3D Rotation folds into Edit > Transform > Reset 3D while the chip is on.
The chip's right click opens the Mac's own menu, as every right click in the app does; the prototype's dark menu is the web page's stand-in for it, with the same rows and divider. Matches otherwise.
A picture's own size is its pixels, so a screenshot that was scaled down to fit when it landed shows a Size dot from the start, and Reset Size puts it at full size. Asked in evaluate.

Reset Size and Reset 3D take any keys on their values with them (a key left behind would put the change back), the way Reset 3D Rotation always did. On a video that removes the animation of that kind; one undo puts it back.
None of these rows has a key: Photoshop gives Skew, Distort, Perspective and the like none, so there was nothing to copy.
